cue: There’s no picture here, only how much light there is, what colour it is, and where it comes from.
rows: A plant has nothing like a lens to focus light into an image. It senses how much light there is, what colour it is, and which direction it comes from.

Plants compare red light with far-red light, a colour just past the edge of what people can see. The balance tells a plant that a neighbour is growing close by, even before the neighbour shades it. Phone cameras capture very little far-red light.
This view removes green, because leaves reflect most green light away, and it smooths out anything quick. Both are the app’s own choices.
